## Natural history notes

A small grass skipper characterized by warm brown to orange-brown wings, pale spots on the forewings, and a compact body with hooked antennae typical of skippers. In Florida, it is found in open grassy habitats such as prairies, pastures, roadsides, lawns, marsh edges, fields, and disturbed areas where grasses are abundant. Adults feed on nectar from low flowers, while the caterpillars feed on grasses, using folded or tied grass blades as shelters while they develop.
